name: Sugar apple (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Sugar apple (Annona squamosa) [Fruits] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DUKE, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 168175 (SR Legacy, Sugar-apples, (sweetsop), raw; NDB 09520) - proximates, vitamins, minerals, fatty-acid fractions, Lys/Trp/Met
Kumar et al., A Review of Nutrition, Bioactivities and Health Benefits of Custard Apple (Annona squamosa), Foods 2025, 14(19):3413 / PMC12523297 (total sugars ~18.15%, mineral & vitamin ranges, Mn)

Yang & Paull, Postharvest physiology and technology of Annona fruits, Food Res. Int. (S0963996911001037) - citric>>malic>isocitric acids; reducing sugars (glucose+fructose) dominate over sucrose; ripe-pulp titratable acidity ~0.29 g/100g
FooDB FOOD00485 (source of the original component list)
provenance.curation_notes: Sugar apple is a SWEET, LOW-ACID fruit: the dominant carbon sources are the free reducing sugars glucose (~7) + fructose (~6) with secondary sucrose (~5 g/100g), ~18 g/100g total sugars. The dominant organic acid is CITRIC (~0.2 g/100g, > malic > isocitric) - completely missing from the original FooDB profile and the single most important gap fixed here. Individual sugar and organic-acid absolutes are literature-derived apportionments (total sugars 18.15%; ripe titratable acidity 0.29 g/100g) an
curation_added: citric acid (~0.20 g/100g - DOMINANT organic acid, was completely absent from FooDB profile)
malic acid (~0.06 g/100g - secondary organic acid, was absent)
quantified individual sugars: D-glucose ~7.0, D-fructose ~6.0, sucrose ~5.0 g/100g (FooDB carried only qualitative 'Sucrose' and 'beta-D-Glucopyranose')
quantified full USDA vitamin/mineral panel amounts (C, B1/B2/B3/B5/B6/B9, K, Ca, Mg, P, Na, Fe, Zn, Cu, Se) plus review-derived Mn
amino-acid amounts (Lys 55, Trp 10, Met 7 mg/100g) and total protein 2.06 g
fatty-acid fraction breakdown and total fat

curation_removed.name: Retinol
curation_removed.reason: preformed (animal-form) vitamin A; does not occur in plant fruit - only provitamin-A carotenoids do. USDA reports 0 RAE for this fruit; FooDB artifact

curation_removed.name: Co2+ / Cobalt
curation_removed.reason: ultratrace, non-nutritive at fruit levels (no cobalamin synthesis in a plant food); FooDB noise, mirrors handling in other plant-food curations

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: ultratrace non-nutritive element, not a growth-relevant nutrient at food concentrations; FooDB noise

curation_removed.name: Iron (Fe3+) / Fe2+ mitochondria (duplicate iron entries)
curation_removed.reason: compartmental BiGG duplicates of the same iron pool; consolidated into a single 'iron' 0.6 mg/100g component

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
